source.title: Mexican wine; Vino de México (Wikipedia)
source.note: Wine regions of Mexico that no register protects, each named as a wine-growing area by a sentence of the English article "Mexican wine" (revision 1374299167, 11 September 2026) or the Spanish "Vino de México" (revision 175727864, 8 October 2026). That sentence is its summary until an article of its own describes its wine, and its names are the ones those sentences give ("Parras" as the English article writes "The wine is produced in Parras, Coahuila"). The Parras Valley lies within La Laguna, as its sentence says. The Valle de Guadalupe is not nested: "Mexican wine" has the San Antonio de las Minas zone include it, while the valley's own articles count San Antonio de las Minas among its parts. San Antonio de las Minas stands at the place OpenStreetMap names "Villa de Juárez (San Antonio de las Minas)". A sentence that names several regions describes none of them: those regions show no summary, and their page links the sentence's article. None is a protected name: the only one Mexico has is Querétaro's (`mx-indicaciones-geograficas.json`). Points are OpenStreetMap's for the place of each name in its state, approximately; La Laguna stands at the Parras Valley, the only part of it named. The Valle de Guadalupe has articles of its own (Wikidata Q834310, "una región vitivinícola localizada en el municipio de Ensenada" in Spanish): they describe it, and its point is Wikidata's.
